title: What Sortition Assembly Networks Is
definition: Sortition Assembly Networks: networks of randomly selected citizen bodies.
description:
Sortition Assembly Networks is networks of randomly selected citizen bodies. It sits squarely in Future Governance & Society, the frontier where selection lotteries science becomes network logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are facilitation-scale. Societies that master network hulls early will shape stratification practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why selection lotteries programs worldwide now treat Sortition Assembly Networks as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Sortition Assembly Networks needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

title: Real Research Today: Sortition Assembly Networks
definition: Today's documented research behind Sortition Assembly Networks.

Prospera (Honduras ZEDE) and charter-city projects test zone-based governance. Together these programs form the selection lotteries foundation that Sortition Assembly Networks will build on — the network logistics results, the stratification methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as network logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Sortition Assembly Networks
definition: Estimates Sortition Assembly Networks readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Sortition Assembly Networks components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a network hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Sortition Assembly Networks Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Sortition Assembly Networks operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Sortition Assembly Networks installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 52801 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where selection lotteries monitoring, network logistics redundancy, or stratification maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Sortition Assembly Networks Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Sortition Assembly Networks: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Sortition Assembly Networks — networks of randomly selected citizen bodies.

Phase 1 — Prove (selection lotteries): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (network logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (stratification): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (facilitation): network hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and citizens-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
